CREATE TABLE athlete
(
	code INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
	name NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
	name_short NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
	name_tv NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
	gender NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
	`function` NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	country_code NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
	country NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	country_full NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	nationality NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	nationality_full NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	nationality_code NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
	height INT NOT NULL,
	weight INT NOT NULL,
	disciplines NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	events NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
	birth_date DATE NOT NULL,
	birth_place NVARCHAR(50),
	birth_country NVARCHAR(50),
	residence_place NVARCHAR(50),
	residence_country NVARCHAR(50),
	nickname NVARCHAR(255),
	hobbies NVARCHAR(255),
	occupation NVARCHAR(50),
	education NVARCHAR(255),
	family NVARCHAR(255),
	lang NVARCHAR(100),
	coach NVARCHAR(100),
	reason TEXT,
	hero TEXT,
	influence TEXT,
	philosophy TEXT,
	sporting_relatives TEXT,
	ritual TEXT,
	other_sports TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE coach
(
	code INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
	name NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
	gender NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
	`function` NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
	category CHAR(1) NOT NULL,
	country_code NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
	country NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	country_full NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	disciplines NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	events NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE event
(
	event NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
	tag NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
	sport NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
	sport_code NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
	sport_url TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE medalist
(
	medal_date DATE NOT NULL,
	medal_type NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
	medal_code INT NOT NULL,
	name NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
	gender NVARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
	country NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	country_code NVARCHAR(5) NOT NULL,
	nationality NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	team NVARCHAR(50),
	team_gender CHAR(1),
	discipline NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	event NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	event_type NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	url_event TEXT NOT NULL,
	birth_date DATE NOT NULL,
	code INT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE medal
(
	medal_type NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
	medal_code INT NOT NULL,
	medal_date DATE NOT NULL,
	name NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	country_code NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
	gender CHAR(1) NOT NULL,
	discipline NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
	event NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	event_type NVARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
	url_event TEXT NOT NULL,
	code NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE medal_total
(
	country_code NVARCHAR(5) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
	Gold_Medal INT NOT NULL,
	Silver_Medal INT NOT NULL,
	Bronze_Medal INT NOT NULL,
	Total INT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE schedule
(
	start_date DATETIME NOT NULL,
	end_date DATETIME,
	day DATE NOT NULL,
	status NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
	discipline NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	discipline_code NVARCHAR(5) NOT NULL,
	event NVARCHAR(10),
	event_medal INT NOT NULL,
	phase NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
	gender CHAR(1) NOT NULL,
	event_type NVARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
	venue NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	venue_code NVARCHAR(5) NOT NULL,
	location_description NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	location_code NVARCHAR(5) NOT NULL,
	url TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE schedule_preliminary
(
	date_start_utc DATETIME NOT NULL,
	date_end_utc DATETIME NOT NULL,
	estimated NVARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
	estimated_start NVARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
	start_text NVARCHAR(5),
	medal INT,
	venue_code NVARCHAR(5) NOT NULL,
	description NVARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
	venue_code_other NVARCHAR(5),
	discription_other NVARCHAR(20),
	team_1_code NVARCHAR(5),
	team_1 NVARCHAR(20),
	team_2_code NVARCHAR(5),
	team_2 NVARCHAR(20),
	tag NVARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
	sport NVARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
	sport_code NVARCHAR(5) NOT NULL,
	sport_url TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE team
(
	code NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
	team NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
	team_gender CHAR(1) NOT NULL,
	country NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
	country_full NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
	country_code NVARCHAR(5) NOT NULL,
	discipline NVARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
	disciplines_code NVARCHAR(5) NOT NULL,
	events NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
	athletes NVARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
	coaches NVARCHAR(255),
	athletes_codes NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
	num_athletes INT NOT NULL,
	coaches_codes NVARCHAR(100),
	num_coaches INT
);

CREATE TABLE torch_route
(
	title NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	city NVARCHAR(50),
	date_start DATETIME NOT NULL,
	date_end DATETIME NOT NULL,
	tag NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
	url TEXT NOT NULL,
	stage_number INT
);

CREATE TABLE venue
(
	venue NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	sports NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
	date_start DATETIME,
	date_end DATETIME,
	tag NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
	url TEXT NOT NULL
);

1) Background / Context
The project focuses on developing a comprehensive data analytics and data warehouse solution for the Paris 2024 Olympic Summer Games. The system will manage and analyze data related to the event, encompassing participating countries, athletes, sports disciplines, medal standings, event details, and more. This repository provides a structured framework for processing and understanding extensive datasets associated with the 2024 Olympics.

 2) Objectives
- To create an efficient data warehouse for storing and managing data related to the Paris 2024 Olympics.
- To provide tools and functionalities for analyzing various aspects of the Olympic data, such as athlete performance, medal standings, and event schedules.
- To support data-driven decision-making and insights generation for stakeholders involved in the Olympics.

 3) Stakeholders & Users
- Olympic Organizing Committee: Oversees the setup and operation of the Olympics, using data for planning and logistics.
- Athletes and Coaches: Access performance data and schedules for strategic preparation and participation.
- Sports Analysts and Journalists: Utilize data insights for reporting and analysis of the event.
- Fans and Spectators: Access event schedules and results.

 4) Functional Descriptions
- Athlete Management: Manage data related to athletes, including personal information, disciplines, and event participation.
- Coach Management: Store and manage coach details and their roles within different sports disciplines.
- Event Schedule and Results: Manage event scheduling, phases, and results tracking, including medal distribution.
- Medal Tracking: Record and analyze medal standings by country and event.
- Team Management: Manage data related to teams, including athletes and coaches details.
- Venue and Torch Route Management: Track venues and torch relay routes with related details and scheduling.
  
 5) Non-Functional Descriptions
- Scalability: The system should efficiently handle large volumes of data related to multiple aspects of the Olympic Games.
- Performance: Ensure quick data retrieval and analysis capabilities.
- Security: Implement robust security measures to protect sensitive data, including personal information of athletes and event details.
- Usability: Provide user-friendly interfaces for different stakeholders to interact with the data system seamlessly.
- Reliability: Ensure data accuracy and system uptime during the Olympic Games period for real-time access.
nl_text: The schemabench_0165 database contains 11 tables, each representing a different entity or relationship in the Olympic Games. The athlete table contains information about the athletes who participate in the games, including their name, gender, function, country, nationality, height, weight, disciplines, events, birth date, birth place, and more. The coach table contains information about the coaches who lead the athletes, including their name, gender, function, country, disciplines, and events. The event table contains information about the events that take place during the games, including the name, tag, sport, and more. The medalist table contains information about the athletes who win medals, including their name, gender, country, nationality, discipline, event, and more. The medal table contains information about the medals that are awarded, including the type, code, date, and more. The medal_total table contains information about the total number of medals awarded by country, including gold, silver, and bronze medals. The schedule table contains information about the schedule of the games, including the start and end dates, day, status, discipline, event, and more. The schedule_preliminary table contains information about the preliminary schedule of the games, including the start and end dates, estimated start time, venue, and more. The team table contains information about the teams that participate in the games, including their name, gender, country, disciplines, events, athletes, and more. The torch_route table contains information about the torch relay route, including the title, city, start and end dates, tag, and more. The venue table contains information about the venues where the events take place, including the name, sports, date, and more.
